followups.problem: The existing smoke changed every goto from waitUntil:'networkidle' to 'domcontentloaded'. On the Classic board page the only wait added is waitForSelector('body') (line 459), which is already true at DOMContentLoaded, and assertMonitorBag runs right after (line 460). Hive and Cockpit at least wait for a JS-rendered shell, but Classic has no such wait.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A Classic-board stylesheet with the wrong content-type, a 404 on a late asset, or a console error thrown by a deferred or async script after DOMContentLoaded lands in classicBag after it has been checked. The smoke stays green where it used to fail, so the flag-off regression guard is weaker than it was on 1.167.32.
followups.fix: Wait for something on the Classic board that its scripts render (for example the board root that board.html's JS fills), or call classicPage.waitForLoadState('load') before assertMonitorBag. If networkidle was dropped because the train 8 live feed keeps a connection open, keep 'load' and not just 'domcontentloaded'.

followups.problem: The keyboard part of the test only shows that PageDown and then Space move scrollY forward. It presses Home, then immediately calls window.scrollTo(0, 0) (line 258) and waits for scrollY === 0, so the programmatic scroll returns the page to the top and Home itself is never checked. The keyboard never reaches the last card, and it is skipped at 390x844.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Suppose Home or End stopped working, for example because a focused card or a keydown handler calls preventDefault, or because an inner scroller takes the key. The test would still pass, since scrollTo(0,0) produces the scrollY === 0 it waits for. The task brief and CHANGELOG say keyboard input reaches the last card and comes back, which the test does not prove.
followups.fix: Remove the page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0)) after Home and wait for scrollY === 0 from the key press alone. Add an End press, or a loop of PageDown presses until state.lastVisible or maxY - y <= 1, then use Home to return. Alternatively, reword the CHANGELOG (see the next item).

followups.problem: This line says 'wheel, touch and keyboard reach the last card and return to the top'. The test only does that for wheel and touch. Keyboard is limited to PageDown and Space moving down, plus a programmatic return, and is not run at 390x844.
followups.exploit_or_failure: The release note claims more test coverage than exists, so a reader would think keyboard reachability and Home are guarded when they are not.
followups.fix: Either strengthen the keyboard steps as in the previous item, or change the line to: 'wheel and touch reach the last card and return to the top, PageDown and Space scroll the page (desktop and tablet sizes)'.

followups.problem: No viewport tests the new 1340/1341 breakpoint. The matrix is 1600, 1280, 800 and 390, and the owner's reported 1440x900 is also missing. 1341 is the narrowest width that still gets the desktop ellipse, now that .hive-shell is width:100% rather than max-content. Its canvas is about 1294-1309 px, so the cards are scaled to about 0.98, and this case is untested. I checked by reading the code: PHONE_MAX uses win.innerWidth (cc-hive-mount.js:592), which includes the scrollbar the same way the (max-width:1340px) media query does. The CSS and JS breakpoints agree, and hiveGeometry keeps rx = cx - cardW/2 - 6 inside the stage. I found no actual failure at the boundary, but nothing guards it.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Several later changes could cause horizontal overflow or a mixed layout at exactly 1341-1355 px: a change to the media query or PHONE_MAX that makes them disagree, a switch to clientWidth or matchMedia on another element, or a header or legend item with white-space:nowrap. For example, the JS could set phone geometry while the CSS still uses absolute ellipse cards. The current matrix would not catch any of these.
followups.fix: Add { width: 1340, height: 900 }, { width: 1341, height: 900 } and { width: 1440, height: 900 } to the viewport list. At 1340 and 1341, assert scrollWidth === clientWidth, and also assert the layout mode: computed position of .hive-card is 'relative' at or below 1340 and 'absolute' above it, with every card's rect inside the .hive-stage rect.

summary: Pass, no blockers. The body lock is gone (command-center.css:19-24). html keeps overflow:visible, so the body's overflow-y:auto carries up to the viewport and the document scrolls. Nothing else on the Hive locks vertical scrolling: the .hive-stage fixed height (cc-hive.css:86) holds only the absolutely placed ellipse cards and becomes height:auto in the grid layout, and the panels below it flow normally. CSS (max-width:1340px) and JS PHONE_MAX=1340 both measure the viewport including the scrollbar (innerWidth), so they agree at 1340/1341. At 1341 and above the desktop ellipse keeps its cards inside the stage, and the shell's width:100%/max-width:1320/margin:auto keeps 1600 centred with the same geometry. In the grid layout the ring overlays are placed from the canvas rect relative to the stage, and !important on position/left/top/transform overrides leftover inline positions after a resize. The flex-wrap and min-width:0 on the header and legend remove the horizontal overflow. The new test uses real mouse.wheel and CDP touch events, waits on domcontentloaded plus the card selector, only dismisses the tour when the Skip button exists, gets the last card from the real .hive-card/.tk selector, and its scrollWidth assertion still measures overflow under overflow-x:hidden. The version bump is consistent across package.json, package-lock, README, the CHANGELOG heading and the release-pin tests. Followups: the Classic smoke lost its load wait when networkidle was replaced; the keyboard check never tests Home (scrollTo masks it) and never reaches the last card, so the CHANGELOG line overstates it; and nothing tests 1340, 1341 or 1440. Limits: I could not read the Cockpit stylesheet or markup, so I cannot rule out inner overflow:hidden or max-height containers in the worker stream or ticket stack. The Cockpit verdict rests on the evidence (wheel and touch reach the last .tk at all four viewports, and scrollWidth equals clientWidth). The train 8 live-feed code is not in the diff and was not re-reviewed.
